subject: Hospitality
title: Coffee as a Profit Center
description: A fast breakdown of Coffee as a Profit Center for builders.

hook.text: A cup of hotel coffee costs $0.30 to brew and sells for $4–6. Coffee has one of the highest markups of any F&B item—over 1,000%.

buildup.text: Hotel coffee programs range from basic drip to full espresso bars with trained baristas.

discovery.text: Partnering with specialty roasters (Stumptown, Illy, Nespresso) adds perceived value. The brand name justifies premium pricing.

twist.text: Free in-room coffee is expected by guests but costs hotels $0.50–1.00 per pod per room per day.

climax.text: Some hotels moved to lobby coffee bars, charging premium prices while eliminating in-room machines.

punchline.text: 30 cents to brew, $5 to sell. Coffee is quietly the hotel's biggest percentage markup.

quiz.question: What is the approximate markup on hotel coffee?
